Bloomberg today published the latest report, providing an in-depth analysis of Apple's Mac product line planning. The report details updates on multiple products including MacBook Pro, MacBook Air, iMac, and more in the coming years.

New MacBook Air, iMac, MacBook Pro and more

Bloomberg points out Apple is targeting the following new Mac releases before the end of this year:

  • New entry-level MacBook Pro with M6 chip
  • New iMac
  • New high-end 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook models with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips and OLED displays

According to the report, the new high-end MacBook models are "on schedule for release sometime between the end of this year and early next year." Apple is testing them with macOS 27.1, which is expected to be released at the end of October.

Apple plans to release updated MacBook Air models in early 2027. The company is also working on a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro with the M7 chip, expected to ship next year.

A new MacBook Neo is also in development, with Apple testing a model featuring the A19 Pro chip. The report says Apple plans to "periodically" release MacBook Neo in new colors.

Apple is also testing Mac mini models with M5 Pro and base M6 processors. New Mac Studio models are also in testing, featuring M5 Max and M5 Ultra processors. Bloomberg specifically notes: "However, the timing and chip and memory configurations for these models will depend on memory chip supply."

Looking further ahead, Bloomberg says the OLED MacBook Air is expected to arrive "as soon as 2028." Apple is also reportedly working on an OLED iMac, which would follow the OLED MacBook Air.

What do you think of Apple's rumored Mac roadmap? Are you planning to upgrade anytime soon? Let us know in the comments.
